newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Former Romanian private bank chief jailed.
newsitem.headline: Former Romanian private bank chief jailed.

text.p: A Romanian court has sentenced the former head of a top private bank to six years in jail on charges of embezzlement and forgery, court officials said on Wednesday.

The Bucharest court of appeals handed down the sentence on Tuesday on Marcel Ivan, former chief executive of Credit Bank. The bank's chief accountant and a top director received lighter sentences as did a businessman involved in illegal dealings.
The court was told Ivan had profited from improper declarations of land sales. He had already served a one-year jail term for receiving unearned income in 1995.

Credit Bank SA, one of Romania's largest private banks set up in 1991, has been in severe financial difficulties and had its banking licence withdrawn by the central bank after failing to mount an acceptable rescue package within a year.
The four convicted men were ordered to pay damages worth the equivalent of $61,000 to Credit Bank.
